content.text: No non-solicit, no-hire, or employee-poaching restriction binding Customer appears anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "solicit", "induce", "hire", "employ", "recruit" return nothing restrictive), and § 12.3 affirmatively confirms Customer made no no-hire commitment and may hire anyone responding to general recruitment. This matches our preferred position, so no redline is needed. (The Customer non-compete in § 12.4 is a separate restrictive-covenant issue outside this rule.)

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or non-inducement covenant binding Customer; targeted searches for "solicit", "induce", "employ", "hire", and "recruit" surface only § 12.3 and unrelated provisions (insurance, definitions). Section 12.3 goes further and expressly preserves Customer's right to hire anyone responding to general recruitment and confirms Customer has made no no-hire commitment. This satisfies the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so no edit is required. The Customer non-compete in § 12.4 is objectionable but falls under a separate non-compete rule, not this non-solicitation rule.
